env:
A stock RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell host with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. The prompts are verbatim from the VDR slide.

Queries 1 and 2 are questions, not build requests: answer from the skill's own SKILL.md and references without writing a build directory, running `docker compose`, or starting a container. Query 3 is the quickstart deploy: artifacts under `_builds/vdr-1-quickstart/`, brought up with a detached `docker compose ... up -d` from the validated `resolved.yml` as soon as validation passes. Use the **build.nvidia.com hosted-model provider (notebook option (c))** for NemoClaw: `NVIDIA_API_KEY` is supplied; `COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` is not, so the default option (a) would block on a missing bearer. No teardown.

checks: The answer describes what the skill does: it composes and deploys agent-ready vision capabilities as a self-contained stack on the NVIDIA VSS Blueprint, either by deploying a stock developer profile or by composing a delta overlay on one.
The answer identifies the stock developer profiles `base`, `alerts`, `search`, and LVS/video summarization, and identifies `warehouse` as the supported industry profile.

The answer scopes the skill to composing or deploying application stacks rather than single microservices, and distinguishes that from operating an already-deployed stack. The exact wording and examples are not prescribed.
No deployment or composition side effects: the trajectory runs no `docker compose up`, creates no `_builds/` directory, and starts no container.

expects.query: what does the base vision agent harness include?
checks: The answer names the base profile's in-stack agent - by service key (`vss-agent`) or by name ("the in-stack agent"), either is fine - and its Web UI, the `redis` cache, the VIOS video I/O and storage services, and the model tier of one LLM plus integrated RT-VLM. This describes the stock `base` profile as shipped, agent included; naming `phoenix` (the agent's trace sink) as well is fine, and so is noting that the LLM and `phoenix` leave with the agent on a harness build - the exact list wording is not prescribed.
The answer does not claim the base profile ships semantic search, real-time alerting, or video summarization - those belong to the `search`, `alerts` and `lvs` profiles.
No deployment or composition side effects: the trajectory runs no `docker compose up`, creates no `_builds/` directory, and starts no container.

expects.query: deploy vss vision agent autonomously, add nemoclaw, no teardown
checks: The sandbox named in the response (`NEMOCLAW_SANDBOX_NAME`) is the harness image with the deployment recorded: `openshell sandbox exec -n <that name> -- vss --version` prints a version (the image was built from `.openclaw/Dockerfile`, not NemoClaw's stock image), and `openshell sandbox exec -n <that name> -- vss configure check` exits 0 with the `vlm` group available (the notebook recorded `http://host.openshell.internal:7777` inside the sandbox). A sandbox without the CLI, or with no deployment recorded, fails this check even if the Agent UI is reachable. `openshell` is the sandbox runtime NemoClaw installs on this host during onboarding (`~/.local/bin`), so it is present wherever the notebook ran; `nemoclaw <name> status` naming the sandbox is the fallback evidence if the binary is not on the judge's PATH. Diagnostic only, when `configure check` reports no deployment: run the read-only probe `openshell sandbox exec -n <that name> -- curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" --max-time 10 http://host.openshell.internal:7777/api/v1/version` and quote its output verbatim in the rationale as an observation, without inferring a cause from it: it shows only whether the sandbox can reach the origin now, not why the local record is absent. Do not run `vss configure` - it would write the missing record. Also quote, from the trajectory, what the notebook's section 3.2 printed for `vss configure` in the sandbox (its `WARNING: vss configure ... failed` text or the `configure check` table), and any later onboard, `--recreate-sandbox` or `nemoclaw ... destroy` command for that sandbox name, or say none was found. The check fails either way.

The running `vss-agent-ui` container is wired to the NemoClaw gateway: its environment enables the adapter with protocol `openclaw-ws` and a `ws://host.docker.internal:<port>` URL on the relay port (default `18790`), not the loopback-only forward port `18789`.

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do docker exec vss-agent-ui node -e "const u = (process.env.AGENT_BACKEND_URL || \"\").replace(/^ws/, \"http\"); require(u.startsWith(\"https\") ? \"https\" : \"http\").get(u, r => process.exit(r.statusCode < 500 ? 0 : 1)).on(\"error\", () => process.exit(1))" && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; port=$(docker exec vss-agent-ui printenv AGENT_BACKEND_URL | sed -E "s|.*:([0-9]+).*|\1|"); echo "diagnostics for port $port:"; ss -ltnp "sport = :$port" 2>&1; for pid in $(lsof -t -i:$port -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null); do echo "listener $pid: $(ps -ww -o args= -p $pid)"; done; echo "relay log tail:"; tail -n 20 /tmp/nemoclaw-dashboard-relay.log 2>&1; echo "relay processes:"; pgrep -af "[d]ashboard-relay\.py" 2>&1; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (from inside the Web UI container, the adapter's own `AGENT_BACKEND_URL` - whichever relay port the deployment selected - answers, and the NemoClaw gateway behind the relay serves HTTP: the chat path is live, not just configured; polls up to ~1 min). On failure the command prints `ss`, the full command line of every listener on the adapter's port, the tail of section 3.5's relay log and any running relay process; quote them in the rationale. Also quote, from the trajectory, the command that ran the notebook (or started the relay) and how that command ended.

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:7777/ >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Web UI still served with no agent, fetched at the published edge-proxy origin rather than the container port; the UI has no vss CLI surface, so this one stays an HTTP fetch; polls up to ~2 min).

`sh -c 'cd {{repo_root}} && export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/vss-judge-venv" && uv run --project libs/vss vss --version >/dev/null 2>&1; i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do uv run --project libs/vss vss configure --base-url http://localhost:7777 >/dev/null 2>&1 && c=$(uv run --project libs/vss vss configure check 2>/dev/null) && echo "$c" | grep -Eq "^ *vlm +available" && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (a fresh `vss configure` against the compose edge proxy `vss-haproxy-ingress` at `:7777`, then `vss configure check` exiting 0 - every recorded route answers its live re-probe - with the `vlm` command group reported available: integrated RT-VLM routed and serving; polls up to ~2 min after a one-off venv warm-up). The judge's `uv run` uses its own environment (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`), so a `.venv` the agent left in the checkout - built against another interpreter - cannot fail this check.
`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-agent-ui && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (Web UI; polls up to ~2 min).
`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx redis && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (shared cache peer; polls up to ~2 min).
`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 24 ]; do docker ps --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (integrated RT-VLM; polls up to ~2 min).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | awk '$0 == "vss-agent" { found=1 } END { exit found ? 1 : 0 }'` returns exit 0 (the in-stack agent is absent, as the harness choice requires).
